I've been working this same 3 mu plot in Quzhou for more than half a century. My father did the same rotation before me — wheat in the cold months, maize in the hot months. That's how it's always been done here. Two people in the household, so the yield from 3 mu is enough to eat and sell a little. I don't take risks with new methods I don't understand.

**Wheat (October sowing, June harvest):**
I'll use the improved variety seed from the county supply store — the same one I've used the past few years. It's reliable. Before sowing, I hire the rotary tiller to turn the soil. I put down base fertilizer — diammonium phosphate and urea mixed in — then top-dress with urea again at jointing in spring. I water three times: once before sowing to prepare the seedbed, once in February when green-up begins, once at heading. I spray herbicide in early winter when weeds emerge and spray once more around heading time for disease. That's what I've always done.

**Maize (June sowing, October harvest):**
Right after the wheat combine leaves, I sow maize directly into the stubble. No point plowing in summer heat — the machine goes straight in. I buy hybrid seed every year, can't reuse it. Summer rains in July and August help a lot, but I water once at planting if the ground is dry and once at tasseling if it hasn't rained enough. I spray herbicide right after sowing before the plants come up, and watch for armyworm or aphids — spray once if I see them. By October it's ready to harvest.
